newsitem.title: ITALY: San Paolo future OPA not ruled out - Consob.
newsitem.headline: San Paolo future OPA not ruled out - Consob.

text.p: The way San Paolo bank's stock offering this month was held was in line with privatisation rules and so there was no need for the Holding of Italy's biggest bank to carry out a public share purchase (OPA), bourse regulator Consob said.

The Holding remains the largest overall shareholder in San Paolo and details of the offer were made known to the public who bought shares, following rules, but if the current shareholding arrangement changed then Consob could review the situation and might oblige the Holding to make an OPA.

The Holding privately placed some 22 percent of the bank with a group of core shareholders, bringing its stake to 45.6 percent, and held a public sale of around 27 percent giving it a stake of some 20 percent.
The core shareholders, who took between two and five percent of ordinary capital, are committed under so-called stability contracts, not to transfer or increase their stakes.
But the situation would change if they modified these accords in the next two years resulting in the Holding losing its role as largest overall shareholder, Consob said.
